problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2z+x-5y=1 \\ -y+5z-4x=-2 \\ 2x-6y-z=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & a \\ b & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & c & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$

examples.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ z-x+2=-1 \\ 2y-2x-4z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083420/assets/c9b7abb2641034c1769c6fe6b13b96edd7ccc282b61424b2031a3d37faa456e4.png)
What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ -x+0y+z=-3 \\ -2x+2y-4z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083420/assets/6f1bf319faf8be4a9a79c0a6f9301e6eac48a5b04f66949b679e8445b07e9d9c.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083420/assets/fc1ac06787ed64ebefbb1a7a82f9bf785525777f61831bbbc39bd25c7e629d5a.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083420/assets/d0249dcecf6b75cd6ff7c4623beac6fd6cfae64a58d043bb6759440167f40ea1.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083420/assets/64d1f57717dda57c8a7fbc403728ee9699a22ce995f68a50a0b80f25543fdab6.png)

Therefore $a=0,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-3.$

feedback.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+2z=0 \\ x+2y+3z=2 \\ 3x+y+z=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & a & 2 \\ b & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0x+y+2z=0 \\ x+2y+3z=2 \\ 3x+y+z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=1,\,b=1,\,c=1.$
